subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should gh-issues hardening land as structured untrusted-content wrapping or summarization first, wait for per-spawn toolsAllow, require sandboxed unattended workers, or bundle those changes together?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable fix changes how tool-enabled workers process external GitHub content and how much child capability isolation the runtime must guarantee.

options.title: Bundle content and child-policy hardening
options.body: Treat issue/comment text as structured untrusted data and pair unattended gh-issues workers with sandbox or per-spawn least-privilege controls once the API shape is accepted.

options.title: Land content boundary first
options.body: Wrap or summarize GitHub text before task construction now, and track child tool isolation through the per-spawn policy issue and PR.

options.title: Wait for spawn policy
options.body: Hold gh-issues changes until maintainers settle the permanent sessions_spawn tool-policy API and then adapt the skill workflow around it.

recommendation.title: Bundle content and child-policy hardening
recommendation.body: Treat issue/comment text as structured untrusted data and pair unattended gh-issues workers with sandbox or per-spawn least-privilege controls once the API shape is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-line blame and prior history tie Peter to both the gh-issues skill surface and the sessions_spawn boundary decision.
